# 2 Samuel Chapter 9 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 177v–178r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_009_page_001.jpg, 2SA_009_page_002.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** David said, "Is there still anyone remaining of the house of Saul, that I may show him covenant-faithfulness for Jonathan's sake?"

**2** Now the house of Saul had a servant whose name was Ziba, and they summoned him to David. The king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" He said, "Your servant is he."

**3** The king said, "Is there not still someone of the house of Saul, that I may show the covenant-faithfulness of God to him?" Ziba said to the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan, crippled in his feet."

**4** The king said to him, "Where is he?" Ziba said to the king, "He is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar."

**5** Then King David sent and brought him from the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.

**6** And Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan, son of Saul, came to David and fell on his face and bowed down. David said, "Mephibosheth!" And he said, "Behold, your servant."

**7** David said to him, "Do not fear, for I will surely show you covenant-faithfulness for the sake of Jonathan your father. I will restore to you all the land of Saul your grandfather, and you shall eat at my table always."

**8** He bowed down and said, "What is your servant, that you should regard a dead dog such as I?"

**9** Then the king summoned Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, "All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to the son of your master.

**10** You shall cultivate the land for him — you and your sons and your servants — and bring in the produce, that the son of your master may have food to eat. But Mephibosheth the son of your master shall eat at my table always." Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

**11** Ziba said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so shall your servant do." So Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's sons.

**12** Mephibosheth had a young son whose name was Mica. And all who dwelt in Ziba's house were servants to Mephibosheth.

**13** So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he ate always at the king's table. He was lame in both his feet.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agree on the structure of this chapter as a self-contained narrative about David's *chesed* toward the house of Saul. The chapter's three-fold repetition of *chesed* (vv.1, 3, 7) and the refrain "at my table" (vv.7, 10, 11, 13) are recognized as the theological and literary framework. The narrative moves from question (v.1) to fulfillment (v.13) with deliberate symmetry. No major textual variants affect this chapter.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "covenant-faithfulness" vs. "faithful love"
- **EMET:** "covenant-faithfulness [chesed]"
- **LOGOS:** "covenant-faithfulness"
- **PNEUMA:** "faithful love"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "covenant-faithfulness" — per project convention. PNEUMA's "faithful love" captures warmth but loses the covenantal dimension that is central to the passage.

### V.2 — "summoned" vs. "called" vs. "brought before"
- **EMET:** "they-called him to David"
- **LOGOS:** "they summoned him"
- **PNEUMA:** "they brought him before David"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "they summoned him to David" — *qara* can mean call/summon; "summoned" fits the royal court context. PNEUMA's "brought before" adds action not in the text.

### V.3 — "crippled in his feet" vs. "stricken of feet" vs. "crippled in both feet"
- **EMET:** "stricken of-feet [nekeh raglayim]"
- **LOGOS:** "crippled in his feet"
- **PNEUMA:** "crippled in both feet"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "crippled in his feet" — *nekeh raglayim* means "stricken/smitten of feet." LOGOS is most precise; PNEUMA's "both feet" anticipates v.13. EMET's "stricken" is too archaic for consensus.

### V.7 — "field" vs. "land"
- **EMET:** "all [the]-field of-Sha'ul"
- **LOGOS:** "all the land of Saul"
- **PNEUMA:** "all the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "all the land of Saul your grandfather" — *sadeh* can mean field or landed estate; "land" is appropriate for royal holdings. PNEUMA's expansion is natural but adds words not in the Hebrew.

### V.7 — "grandfather" vs. "father"
- **EMET:** "your-grandfather [literally: father]"
- **LOGOS:** "your grandfather"
- **PNEUMA:** "your grandfather Saul"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "your grandfather" — Hebrew *avikha* literally means "your father" but here refers to Saul, who was Mephibosheth's grandfather. English convention requires "grandfather" to avoid confusion.

### V.8 — "turned to" vs. "show regard to" vs. "notice"
- **EMET:** "you-have-turned to the-dead dog"
- **LOGOS:** "you should show regard to a dead dog"
- **PNEUMA:** "you would notice a dead dog like me"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "you should regard a dead dog such as I" — *panah* means "turn toward/regard." LOGOS's formal register fits the court setting. PNEUMA's "notice" is too casual for the gravity of the self-abasement.

### V.10 — "bread" vs. "food" vs. "harvest"
- **EMET:** "bread [lechem]"
- **LOGOS:** "bread to eat"
- **PNEUMA:** "food"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "food to eat" — *lechem* can mean "bread" or "food" generally. In context, the produce of farmland is broader than bread alone. "Food" is clearer while LOGOS's "to eat" (*le-ekhol*) is present in the Hebrew.

### V.11 — "at my table" (speaker ambiguity)
- **EMET:** preserves the awkward MT with David's speech inserted
- **LOGOS:** smooths into narration: "So Mephibosheth ate at David's table"
- **PNEUMA:** "And so Mephibosheth ate at David's table"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "So Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's sons." Following LOGOS/PNEUMA in reading the final clause as narration. The MT is textually awkward (see EMET's note), and the consensus rendering preserves the meaning without the ambiguity.

### V.12 — "dwelling" vs. "who dwelt" vs. "living"
- **EMET:** "all [the]-dwelling of-[the]-house of-Tsiva"
- **LOGOS:** "all who dwelt in Ziba's house"
- **PNEUMA:** "everyone living in Ziba's household"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "all who dwelt in Ziba's house" — LOGOS best captures *moshav bet Tsiva*. PNEUMA's "everyone living in" is natural but loses the Hebrew construction.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
